text:
samira: Hey team :wave: Medix POC — they want Redwood Private via an interface VPCE in us-west-2 for a short Dedicated-pool POC. Can someone list the absolute minimal network checklist and common gotchas? They gave VPC CIDR 10.10.0.0/16 and three private subnets (10.10.1.0/24, 10.10.2.0/24, 10.10.3.0/24).

olivia: Quick top-level: 1) Interface VPCE for the service (us-west-2) with Private DNS ON if they want api.redwood.example to resolve. 2) Security group on the VPCE must allow inbound 443 from the subnets. 3) Outbound NAT for subnets (to reach our hosted control-plane endpoints during bootstrapping) OR explicit route to our peered endpoint if using peering. 4) Route tables must not block return traffic (no overly strict NACLs). :white_check_mark:

marc: Important detail — interface endpoints DO NOT traverse VPC peering or TGW by default. If their Redwood Private control plane is in our provider account and they plan to use VPC peering, that won't reach an interface VPCE. For cross-account PrivateLink we expose an Endpoint Service (NLB) and they create an Interface VPCE in their account. Confirm whether Medix is in the same account as their infra or separate account. :thinking_face:

jia: Minimal subnet requirements for Dedicated pools we ask for during POC: 3 private subnets in distinct AZs, each with at least /24. Instances must be able to egress to our onboarding endpoints on 443. If they have strict egress rules we provide a short allowlist (IPs + FQDNs).

samira: They said same account — good. They also asked about hosted API keys vs Private onboarding keys. Short answer: for Private we exchange a bootstrap token during provisioning and they get a customer-scoped key that is stored in their KMS; hosted API keys are not used for Private nodes. We'll send the bootstrap token flow doc.

marc: Typical gotchas I've seen during POCs: 
- No NAT (0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-xxxx) so init fails when agents try to pull images / contact control plane.
- Endpoint SG restricts ephemeral ports (Redwood agents use outbound ephemeral ports for TLS handshake; inbound on the VPCE SG only needs 443).
- Private DNS not enabled so the SDK hits the public hostname and fails.
- Route table points to an appliance that drops 443 to our IPs.

olivia: Add this troubleshooting CLI to ask them to run before the pre-check:

```
aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0abc1234567890 --region us-west-2
aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0abc1234567890 --region us-west-2
# check for nat gateways
aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways --filter Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0abc1234567890 --region us-west-2
```

marc: Also ask them to paste the VPCE security group rules. Minimal SG: allow inbound TCP 443 from 10.10.0.0/16, outbound allow established (or 0.0.0.0/0). Example: 

```
Inbound:
- Type: HTTPS, Protocol: TCP, Port: 443, Source: 10.10.0.0/16
Outbound:
- All traffic, 0.0.0.0/0
```

jia: Private DNS note: if they enable private DNS on the VPCE, the service DNS name (e.g., private-api.redwood-internal.example) will resolve to ENI IPs — ensure their resolver rules or Route53 Resolver rules don't override.

samira: They just ran a quick test and saw "connect timeout" from a lambda in the same VPC. Is that consistent with a missing route or SG?

marc: Connect timeout usually means either: 1) SG denies, 2) NACL denies, 3) DNS resolves to wrong IP (public) and egress blocked. If it's a Lambda in the same VPC, check the lambda's subnet route table: does it route 0.0.0.0/0 to a NAT? Lambdas in private subnets require NAT for outbound HTTPS.

olivia: For the security questionnaire bits they asked: "Does data plane egress to public internet?" Answer: For Redwood Private using Interface VPCE + Endpoint Service, control-plane registration and health-checks occur over the VPCE. If you choose to allow egress to our hosted control plane, it uses TLS to our endpoints; otherwise traffic stays inside PrivateLink. We'll provide an allowlist if they disallow DNS/FQDNs.

infra-bot: deploy/edge-proxy-checker #198 succeeded — no issues on our service side.

samira: Next steps: I'll run a 15-minute pre-check with Medix tomorrow 10:00 PT. Can @marc and @olivia join to look at route tables and SGs? I'll ask them to run those aws cli commands and paste outputs here before the meeting.

marc: I'll be there. Also prepare the small allowlist of IPs/FQDNs — I have the latest list, will paste it in the meeting.

olivia: I'll draft the minimal steps doc (one-pager) and include the bootstrap token flow + example route table and SG snippets. Will drop link once ready. :+1:

samira: Awesome, thanks. If pre-check shows NAT missing we'll ask them to create one and update route tables — common quick fix.

jia: FYI if they later switch to TGW we have a config note: you must front our Endpoint Service with an NLB in the provider account and confirm TGW attachment can reach the NLB subnets. TGW specifics are more involved; for POC we recommend direct VPCE in the customer account.

samira: Perfect. I'll update Medix and post results here after the call. :rocket:
